Otho hands the player The Earl of Omonporch.
Saad Amus, who haunts Bethesda Susa, is a boss-tier fighter.
Joppa is where you'll find Argyve.
The Villagers of Joppa bear an old grudge against the Girsh.

Kun opens their eyes for the first time in Joppa.

Argyve, hunched over the cluttered workbench where he has muttered at half-built gadgets for the better part of a lifetime, finally presses on the newcomer the job he calls Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!.
Barathrum the Old, who gathered the faithful in secret in the canyon hideout for generations before any wanderer ever stumbled upon its gates, is counted among the Barathrumites.
Tomb of the Eaters, a perilous quest that sends adventurers through sultans' reliquaries and into the deepest mysteries of Qud's buried history, unfolds from first step to last within Eaters' Tomb.
Kun, waking with no memory of the road, surrounded by the smell of salt and reed while unfamiliar faces turn to watch from the leaning huts, first opens his eyes in Joppa.
Barathrum the Old, more than the crawling horrors of the deep and more than any other impurity their patrols have put to the sword across the generations, is despised by the Putus Templar.

The Earl of Omonporch, a quest that opens with nothing but rumor and drifting hearsay yet ends, if the wanderer's luck holds, in genuine discovery, sends the player to find Asphodel Earl of Omonporch.
Reclamation, no errand for the half-prepared, keeps its doors shut and its grim work refusing to begin until the older matter has been seen through, and that older matter is The Golem.

The Joppa Recoiler, salvage that looks like junk at a glance yet is prized dearly by seasoned wanderers who know what the trinket can really do, is handed out as the reward for solving Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!.

Joppa, the low quiet settlement in the southern marsh whose reed-ringed huts see travelers drift through year after year while only a rare few put down roots, counts among its people the old tinker Argyve.
Barathrum the Old, who has answered to many names across his unnaturally long years, scholar and exile and heretic among them, is in blood and bone an Urshiib.
Bethesda Susa, a ruin far off past ash and older ruin that almost no outsider has ever laid eyes upon and fewer still have walked out of, keeps hidden in its buried depths the Temple of the Rock.
The Girsh, demons that clawed their way up from below to become a blight upon every living thing that heroes have ever sworn to protect, were fought in the bloody reckoning called Reclamation.

Barathrum the Old, fretting for many seasons over the friend who wandered into the bright tangle of the wood and pressing the question on anyone who would listen, at last hands the matter over as the task called Pax Qlanq, I Presume?.

The Scrapped Waydroid, a ruined half-sunk heap long forgotten by the world yet wanted badly enough that someone will pay to send you digging after it, is the thing you are sent to recover in More Than a Willing Spirit.

Otho, who keeps the old rites and older grudges of his order alive and says little to strangers until they have earned a measure of his trust, holds out to the worthy a sober charge he calls A Call to Arms.

Baetyl, that strange engine sheltered among relics and machine-spirits by a faith that reveres the works of metal above all flesh and keeps its saints close, is held in special favor by the Mechanimists.

Golgotha, where a thousand years of refuse has been packed down into the dark and few of those who climb in ever manage to climb back out, plays host to the grim trial known as More Than a Willing Spirit.
Reseph, who speaks to the kneeling faithful in a voice like grinding iron and who was once, perhaps, only a machine among machines, now serves as a sworn member of the Seraphic Covenant.

The alchemist, patient and unhurried in a back room far from the noise of the world, mixing acrid draughts for people who come seeking cures and leave carrying riddles, makes a home within Bethesda Susa.
Otho, after long years of labor in tunnels that began as a bolt-hole gouged into the canyon wall and grew into workshop, sanctuary and fortress against the world above, simply calls Grit Gate home.

The metamorphic polygel, a shimmering ooze that rewrites whatever it touches and is coveted by adventurers past all reason and all good sense, comes at the very end as the reward for completing Tomb of the Eaters.

The Villagers of Joppa, who keep long memories and few powerful friends while minding their own marsh and asking little of any outsider, will never forgive one foe, and that foe is the demon-brood called the Girsh.

Decoding the Signal, one link in a longer chain of labor that the elders warn will lead you nowhere at all until the older work is safely behind you, stays locked until More Than a Willing Spirit is done.
Starformed Ehalcodon, which descended in a fall of cold light so vast and wrong against the sky that the lesser horrors of the deep gathered at once to name it kin, is in the end one of the Girsh.

Herodododicus, who rattles off riddles to anyone who pauses in the dark and has waited there delighting in his own cleverness for a very long time, has become the very thing that Tomb of the Eaters sends you out to seek.

In his cramped workshop at Joppa, Argyve - a Mutated Human and low-tier merchant sworn to the Barathrumites - sets the player on Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!, the puzzle that sends them hunting a coil of Copper Wire and pays out, at its end, with a Joppa Recoiler.

Barathrum the Old, the Urshiib elder who dwells in Grit Gate and leads the Barathrumites, hands down Tomb of the Eaters - a descent into the Eaters' Tomb that cannot start until 'Pax Qlanq, I Presume?' is done and ends with a dollop of metamorphic polygel.

Otho, the Urshiib tinker holed up in Grit Gate among the Barathrumites, throws three jobs your way at once - A Call to Arms, Decoding the Signal and The Earl of Omonporch - and is himself the quarry you must track down in A Canticle for Barathrum.

Down in the bright snarl of the Rainbow Wood lurks Pax Qlanq, a Fungi creature of level 30 and 300 HP and the very thing 'Pax Qlanq, I Presume?' sends you to find; Barathrum the Old sets that task, it unfolds in those same woods, and it pays out a quantum mote.

The Temple of the Rock, tucked inside Bethesda Susa, shelters Phinae Hoshaiah High Priest of the Rock - a Mutated Human boss-tier fighter who keeps faith with the Mechanimists - alongside the strange machine Baetyl.

text: Reseph, the towering Robot preached over at Starfarers' Quay - a level-100 colossus with 4000 HP - is sworn to the Seraphic Covenant yet adored by the Mechanimists; recovering him is the heart of We Are Starfreight, a quest Barathrum the Old assigns.

Slog of the Cloaca, the Mollusk boss-tier fighter festering at the bottom of Golgotha, shares that pit with the trial More Than a Willing Spirit, which Otho sets, sends you after a Scrapped Waydroid, and rewards with Sparafucile's Carbine.

Asphodel Earl of Omonporch, a Sentient Plant who holds court at Omonporch, is the prize of The Earl of Omonporch - a hunt Otho hands out that plays out in that very place and only opens once Decoding the Signal is finished.
Kun, the wanderer who first wakes in Joppa, is beloved of the Barathrumites but marked for death by both the Girsh and the Putus Templar.
A Canticle for Barathrum, set in Grit Gate and handed over by Argyve, sends the player to find Otho and cannot even begin until Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka! is behind them.
Sparafucile, the Urshiib who works Grit Gate as a mid-tier merchant, runs with the Barathrumites; Sparafucile's Carbine is the payoff for seeing More Than a Willing Spirit through.

Saad Amus, a level-35 boss-tier fighter with 350 HP, keeps to Bethesda Susa, sharing that buried place with the alchemist - a Mutated Human of level 30 and 175 HP who works as a high-tier merchant and also brawls as a non-boss fighter. Boss-rank fighters carry the boss flag set true, the non-boss role false, and Bethesda Susa itself hosts Decoding the Signal.
Decoding the Signal, which Otho assigns, drives the player to dig the robot Baetyl out of the Temple of the Rock, throws them against the Mechanimists, and must wait on More Than a Willing Spirit.
The Golem, a quest Barathrum the Old entrusts to you from Grit Gate, hinges on recovering neutron flux and stays sealed until Tomb of the Eaters is complete.

Reclamation, run out of Omonporch and handed down by Barathrum the Old, hurls you against the Girsh, the Putus Templar and the monstrous Starformed Ehalcodon, and cannot begin before The Golem is done.
Among the Barathrumites stand Argyve and Otho, both liked by the order, and Barathrum the Old himself - the Urshiib elder of Grit Gate - while Golem, a non-boss fighter, rounds out their number.
The Girsh, who hate the Barathrumites, the Mechanimists, the Putus Templar and the Villagers of Joppa alike, claim the fallen titan Starformed Ehalcodon as a member and once fought in Reclamation.
Grit Gate, three strata down, shelters Barathrum the Old, Otho, Sparafucile and Golem, and out of its tunnels come three trials at once - A Call to Arms, A Canticle for Barathrum and The Golem.

Phinae Hoshaiah High Priest of the Rock, a Mutated Human of level 20 and 225 HP who lives at the Temple of the Rock and fights as a boss-tier fighter, belongs to the Mechanimists and is held dear by them; that same cult once clashed in Decoding the Signal.

text: Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!, the puzzle Argyve sets at Rust Wells, has you turn up a length of Copper Wire - weightless and worth nothing - and rewards you with a Joppa Recoiler, worth 25 and weighing 1, once it's solved.
We Are Starfreight, Barathrum the Old's commission, ranges across both Omonporch and Starfarers' Quay in search of the robot Reseph and only unlocks after Reclamation.

The Seraphic Covenant counts two among its own - Barathrum the Old, who also keeps faith with the Barathrumites, and the robot Reseph - even as the Putus Templar nurse hatred for the Barathrumites, the Girsh and the Mechanimists.
A Call to Arms, set in Grit Gate and given by Otho, pits the player against the Putus Templar - who themselves fought in it - and only opens after The Earl of Omonporch is wrapped up.

Starformed Ehalcodon - a Girsh Nephilim of level 60 and 12000 HP that fights as a boss-tier fighter and runs with the Girsh - is one of the foes Reclamation throws at you, and it played its part in that same battle.

The Urshiib bloodline runs through three of the Barathrumites - Barathrum the Old, Otho and Sparafucile - while the Mutated Human strain claims Argyve, the alchemist and Phinae Hoshaiah High Priest of the Rock.

Barathrum the Old, familiar to anyone who has spent even a single season trading news and water along the roads of the wastes, is a member of Barathrumites.
A Call to Arms, which is unlocked by The Earl of Omonporch, is given by Otho, requires fighting Putus Templar and takes place in Grit Gate.
A Canticle for Barathrum, which is set in Grit Gate, follows Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!, is given by Argyve and asks the player to find Otho.
Argyve, who is of the Mutated Human race, entrusts the player with Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!, dwells in Joppa, enjoys the favor of Barathrumites and fills the role of a low-tier merchant.
Asphodel Earl of Omonporch, who is the target of The Earl of Omonporch, is a Sentient Plant by lineage and resides in Omonporch.
Baetyl, who is the target of Decoding the Signal, makes a home in Temple of the Rock, enjoys the favor of Mechanimists, carries 2000 HP and stands at level 25.
Barathrum the Old, who makes a home in Grit Gate, assigns the quest The Golem, assigns the quest Pax Qlanq, I Presume?, is a member of Seraphic Covenant and belongs to Barathrumites.
The Barathrumites, which includes Argyve in its ranks, includes Sparafucile in its ranks and despises Girsh.
Bethesda Susa, which is home to Saad Amus, is the setting of Decoding the Signal, contains Temple of the Rock, is home to alchemist and lies at strata 0.
Decoding the Signal, which occurs in Temple of the Rock, requires finding Baetyl and follows More Than a Willing Spirit.
The boss-tier fighter, which is held by Starformed Ehalcodon, is held by Saad Amus and is the part played by Slog of the Cloaca.
The Girsh, which is hostile to Mechanimists, is hostile to Villagers of Joppa, numbers Starformed Ehalcodon among its members, is battled during Reclamation and is hostile to Putus Templar.
Golem, who belongs to Barathrumites, resides in Grit Gate, acts as a non-boss fighter, has 350 HP and is level 50.
Grit Gate, which is inhabited by Sparafucile, stages A Call to Arms, stages The Golem, is inhabited by Otho and lies at strata 3.
Kun, who is disliked by Girsh, first appears in Joppa, enjoys the favor of Barathrumites and is held in low regard by Putus Templar.
The Mechanimists, which holds Reseph in esteem, is fought in Decoding the Signal and counts Phinae Hoshaiah High Priest of the Rock as a member.

text: Omonporch, which harbors Reclamation, harbors The Earl of Omonporch, is inhabited by Asphodel Earl of Omonporch, is the setting of We Are Starfreight and lies at strata 0.
Otho, who is a member of Barathrumites, must be found in A Canticle for Barathrum, is of the Urshiib race, gives the player the quest More Than a Willing Spirit, has 95 HP and has reached level 28.
Pax Qlanq, who is a Fungi by lineage, resides in Rainbow Wood, is the target of Pax Qlanq, I Presume?, has 300 hitpoints and is level 30.
Pax Qlanq, I Presume?, which grants quantum mote, asks the player to find Pax Qlanq, is given by Barathrum the Old and is set in Rainbow Wood.

Phinae Hoshaiah High Priest of the Rock, who serves as a boss-tier fighter, is a member of Mechanimists, belongs to the Mutated Human race, enjoys the favor of Mechanimists, carries 225 HP and is level 20.

text: The Putus Templar, which is hostile to Mechanimists, is battled during A Call to Arms, is fought in Reclamation, despises Barathrumites and looks down on Kun.
Reclamation, which requires fighting Putus Templar, comes from Barathrum the Old, calls for battle with Starformed Ehalcodon and requires completing The Golem.
Reseph, who lives in Starfarers' Quay, belongs to Seraphic Covenant, is favored by Mechanimists, has reached level 100 and carries 4000 HP.
Slog of the Cloaca, who lives in Golgotha, fills the role of a boss-tier fighter, is of the Mollusk race, carries 150 HP and has reached level 17.
Sparafucile, who belongs to Barathrumites, makes a home in Grit Gate, works as a mid-tier merchant, belongs to the Urshiib race, has reached level 24 and has 95 hitpoints.
Starformed Ehalcodon, who is a Girsh Nephilim by lineage, is a member of Girsh, is battled during Reclamation, stands at level 60 and carries 12000 HP.
Temple of the Rock, which stages Decoding the Signal, is inhabited by Phinae Hoshaiah High Priest of the Rock, is inhabited by Baetyl and lies at strata 16.

text: The Earl of Omonporch, which unfolds in Omonporch, is given by Otho and requires completing Decoding the Signal.
The Golem, which requires completing Tomb of the Eaters, sends the player to locate neutron flux and is offered by Barathrum the Old.
Tomb of the Eaters, which awards metamorphic polygel, occurs in Eaters' Tomb, is assigned by Barathrum the Old, follows Pax Qlanq, I Presume? and sends the player to locate Herodododicus.
Urshiib, which numbers Otho among its kind, counts Barathrum the Old among its members and counts Sparafucile among its members.
We Are Starfreight, which is set in Starfarers' Quay, is assigned by Barathrum the Old, is unlocked by Reclamation, asks the player to find Reseph and is set in Omonporch.
Weirdwire Conduit... Eureka!, which takes place in Rust Wells, rewards the player with Joppa Recoiler and requires finding Copper Wire.
The alchemist, who is a Mutated Human by lineage, lives in Bethesda Susa, serves as a non-boss fighter, is level 30 and carries 175 HP.
A Call to Arms, which occurs in Grit Gate, requires fighting Putus Templar, is unlocked by The Earl of Omonporch and is offered by Otho.
A Canticle for Barathrum, which requires finding Otho, takes place in Grit Gate and comes from Argyve.
Argyve, who offers the quest A Canticle for Barathrum, belongs to the Mutated Human race, is liked by Barathrumites, works as a low-tier merchant, carries 150 HP and stands at level 22.
Asphodel Earl of Omonporch, who resides in Omonporch, is of the Sentient Plant race, must be found in The Earl of Omonporch, stands at level 30 and has 500 HP.
Baetyl, who enjoys the favor of Mechanimists, must be found in Decoding the Signal, lives in Temple of the Rock, stands at level 25 and has 2000 HP.
Barathrum the Old, who belongs to the Urshiib race, offers the quest We Are Starfreight, entrusts the player with Reclamation and dwells in Grit Gate.
The Barathrumites, which numbers Golem among its members, favors Otho, favors Argyve and is hostile to Mechanimists.
Bethesda Susa, which stages Decoding the Signal, is home to alchemist, houses Saad Amus and is found at strata 0.
Decoding the Signal, which requires finding Baetyl, is set in Bethesda Susa, takes place in Temple of the Rock and is assigned by Otho.
The boss-tier fighter, which is held by Saad Amus, is held by Slog of the Cloaca and is the part played by Starformed Ehalcodon.
The Girsh, which scorns Kun, is at war with Mechanimists, includes Starformed Ehalcodon in its ranks and is at war with Barathrumites.
Golem, who makes a home in Grit Gate, serves as a non-boss fighter, is part of Barathrumites, carries 350 HP and stands at level 50.
Grit Gate, which shelters Otho, hosts the quest A Call to Arms, is home to Golem, harbors A Canticle for Barathrum and is inhabited by Sparafucile.
Kun, who first appears in Joppa, is disliked by Girsh, is favored by Barathrumites and is disliked by Putus Templar.
